records.title: EAGLE-4 0.1.2 falls back to plain SGLang decoding at high load and posts TokenSpeed tokens/s

primary_event_date.basis: GitHub commit daeb41e documents 0.1.2 images; prior 0.1.2 behavior change commit df5a23a is 2026-10-23T01:36:47Z. Version 0.1.3 was released by commit e110d1e on 2026-10-27T03:19:47Z.

reported_facts: The 0.1.2 notes describe per-batch SGLang fallback to plain decoding and list measured throughput conditions.
Those same notes state the TokenSpeed engine build from that release was withdrawn; the current 0.1.3 notes describe a later TokenSpeed release.
publisher_interpretation: New Runtime summarizes a near-parity high-load SGLang recipe and low-load speedups; the raw release notes say this requires a four-GPU setup and note the ordinary one-GPU quick-start can be slower above roughly 32–64 concurrency.

analyst_inference.text: The 0.1.2 mechanism is historically supported, but the item is stale as of the Nov 8 publication because 0.1.3 had shipped on Oct 27; EAGLE-4 is an inference-serving system, not an agent harness or message-delivery system.
analyst_inference.label: inference

limitations: Benchmark values are vendor release-note claims, not independently reproduced here.
TokenSpeed data must not be read as an available 0.1.2 engine build; the release explicitly says that build was withdrawn.
contradictions: The selected article reports 0.1.2 on Nov 8 despite an official 0.1.3 release on Oct 27; the high-load mechanism may still be present but the version focus is stale.
records.recheck_condition: Use current release 0.1.3 or newer and its own support matrix; rerun the benchmark only with matched hardware, load, engine, and no-spec baseline.
